about: CHAIN kentish_revolt_796 (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/kentish_revolt_796.md; words Data/writing/chain_kentish_revolt_796.json). Kent rises against Mercia under Eadberht Praen after Offa's death, 796 to 798, and the Wantsum ports (Sarre, Fordwic, Dofras) are caught in it: whose tally to pay on, whom to sell spearheads and corn to, whose letters to carry, and what comes after when Coenwulf wins. Fourteen cards, August 796 to 800. Step flags ch_kentish_revolt_796_1 .. _10; side flags ch_kentish_revolt_796_kent, ch_kentish_revolt_796_mercia, ch_kentish_revolt_796_corn, ch_kentish_revolt_796_read, ch_kentish_revolt_796_offer, ch_kentish_revolt_796_pilot; endings ch_kentish_revolt_796_end_mercia (what happened), ch_kentish_revolt_796_end_kent (what happened, from the losing side), ch_kentish_revolt_796_end_both (the two-faced man's reckoning) and ch_kentish_revolt_796_end_spared (history changed: changed_kent_798_spared). Every ending also sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_done. Every option's note names its outcome text. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Sarre, Dofras or Fordwic from August 796 to June 798). Two men at the toll bench with two tallies: the old king's toll man and a thegn's man of the new king of Kent. Sources: Offa died 29 July 796 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 794 for 796; chronicle_793.json 796-07-29-offa-dies); Eadberht Praen took Kent and Archbishop Aethelheard fled (chronicle_793.json 796-summer-eadberht-kent); the toll at Sarre and Fordwic was the king's own right and went by the ship (Sawyer 29, dossiers/sarre.md); 'nobody at the toll place is sure whose toll it is' (places/sarre.json, era 796-798). Two tallies on one bench are ours (?). People: the old toll man is the port's (at Sarre Dunwalh, sarre.tollman); Heahred is invented (Heah- + -red). Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_1 and ch_kentish_revolt_796_paid_mercia or ch_kentish_revolt_796_paid_kent.

cards.note: Step 2 (scheduled 5 days after step 1; the first call at Lundenwic after it, before July 798). The Mercian wic-reeve wants eyes in Kent and no iron going there. Sources: the wic-reeve of Lundenwic (laws of Hlothhere and Eadric c. 16); Offa's son Ecgfrith reigned 141 days and Coenwulf was king by December 796 (chronicle_793.json 796-12-cenwulf-king); the rising probably began in earnest after Ecgfrith's death (Kirby, Earliest English Kings, p. 178, through Wikipedia 'Coenwulf of Mercia'). That a reeve asked merchants for word, and that the Wantsum trade then came round to the Strand, are ours (?). Cast: cast.wighelm. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_2; ch_kentish_revolt_796_mercia if the player agrees to be his eyes; ch_kentish_revolt_796_covered if he lies for Kent.

cards.note: Step 3 (scheduled 3 days after step 1 at Fordwic, Canterbury's landing; also drawn there for anyone on the chain, before July 798). The new king's steward shows the new penny and wants iron or corn. Sources: pennies in Eadberht's name were struck at Canterbury (chronicle_793.json 796-summer-eadberht-kent, note); his moneyers are said to be Babba, Aethelmod and Iaenberht (from memory, not opened tonight (?)); Fordwic has the mint in npc_roles_793.json; Eadberht had been in exile under King Charles's protection (Wikipedia 'Eadberht III Praen'; Charles to Offa, 796, on the exiled priest Odberht, MGH Epistolae IV no. 100, if he is the same man (?)). Spearheads 40 d the bundle of ten (goods_793.json). People: Osnoth the steward is invented (Os- + -noth); the moneyer is unnamed. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_3; ch_kentish_revolt_796_kent (arms) or ch_kentish_revolt_796_corn.

cards.note: Step 4 (drawn at Quentovic in 797 or early 798 for anyone on the chain). The guest master of Saint-Josse has a letter from Abbot Alcuin to the people of Kent. Sources: Alcuin wrote in 797 to the people of Kent urging them to take their archbishop back, and lamented that scarcely anyone was left of the old stock of kings (MGH Epistolae IV no. 129, through Story, Carolingian Connections, p. 145, in Wikipedia 'Coenwulf of Mercia': our rendering, not a quotation); he also wrote to Aethelheard about his flight (no. 128 (?)). The cell of Saint-Josse near Quentovic was given to Alcuin for the lodging of travellers (places/quentovic.json; places/dofras.json story dofras.archbishops_chest). The priest Odberht among the exiles under the king's protection: Charles to Offa, 796 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 100), often taken to be Eadberht (?). How the letter crossed is not recorded: the Frisian boat is ours. People: Osmund is quentovic.osmund (invented). Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_4; carrying sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_letter; staying to hear it sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_knows_letter.

cards.note: Step 6 (scheduled by step 4 at Fordwic; also drawn there while the letter is aboard). Where the letter is to be heard. Sources: Alcuin's letter of 797 to the people of Kent (as step 4); Christ Church was probably plundered in the rising (Kirby, p. 178, through Wikipedia 'Coenwulf of Mercia') (?). Letters to a people were read out; that this one was read at a church door in Canterbury is ours (?). People: Wigheard, a priest of Christ Church who stayed, is invented (Wig- + -heard); Osnoth as step 3. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_6 and ch_kentish_revolt_796_letter_done, clears ch_kentish_revolt_796_letter; an open reading sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_read (the road to the changed ending).

cards.note: Step 7, a turn (drawn at Dofras in 797 or early 798 for anyone on the chain). The Mercian king's reeve is gone from the bench and Eadberht's man hires the boat for a tide's lightering, and asks in what you will be paid. Sources: the reeve of Dofras 'changes, and changes again' (places/dofras.json, era 797-825; its reeve Hereberht, Offa's man, is invented); Eadberht's pennies were good silver of Offa's heavy standard as far as is known (?), so by weight they were worth what any penny was after he fell: the fear is real, the loss is not. Weaving at Dover (places/dofras.json). People: Ealdhun, Eadberht's man, is invented (Eald- + -hun); Beornflaed is dofras.alewife. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_7; ch_kentish_revolt_796_praen_coin if paid in the new pennies.

cards.note: Step 8 (drawn at Lundenwic from January to June 798 for anyone on the chain). The pope's answer has come and the king will go into Kent this summer. Sources: Coenwulf wrote to Pope Leo III asking that the southern archbishopric be moved to London; Leo refused, and cast Eadberht out of the Church as a priest who had made himself king (Leo III to Coenwulf, 798, Haddan and Stubbs, Councils III; chronicle_793.json 798-leo-canterbury; English Historical Documents no. 205 through Wikipedia 'Coenwulf of Mercia': our rendering, not a quotation). The comparison with Julian the Apostate is from memory of that letter (?). The army went in 798; the season is not recorded (the chronicle table fires it at midsummer) (?). Where Aethelheard waited is not recorded: the game has him at Lundenwic under the Mercian king (spine, cast.aethelheard) (?). The archbishop's offer of a penitent's life for a kingdom laid down is ours: it is the door to the changed ending and opens only if the letter was read openly (ch_kentish_revolt_796_read). Cast: cast.wighelm, cast.aethelheard. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_8; ch_kentish_revolt_796_mercia with ch_kentish_revolt_796_pilot, or ch_kentish_revolt_796_offer, or ch_kentish_revolt_796_kent with ch_kentish_revolt_796_warned.

cards.note: Step 9, the hard road only (scheduled 4 days after step 8 at Sarre, before August 798 and before the army comes). The offer is put to a tonsured king in the ferryman's hut. Sources: Eadberht had been a priest (the byname Praen; Leo III's letter of 798); he had lived in exile among the Franks (as step 3); what really followed was his capture and maiming (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 796 for 798). This meeting, the offer and his going are invented: it is where the player may change history. Success sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_spared and changed_kent_798_spared and schedules the changed ending; failure sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_offer_refused and the story goes on to step 10. People: Eadberht Praen is historical (king of Kent 796 to 798); Heahred as step 1. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_9.

cards.note: Step 10 (drawn at Sarre, Dofras or Fordwic from July 798 through 799, unless Kent was spared). The Mercian army is in Kent. Sources: 'Cynewulf [Cenwulf], King of Mercia, made inroads upon the inhabitants of Kent as far as the marsh; and the Mercians seized Edbert Pryn, their king, led him bound into Mercia' (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 796 for 798, tr. J. Ingram, 1823; quoted in the intention and the news); the same annal adds that his eyes were put out and his hands cut off; the Marsh is Romney Marsh, the land of the Merscware (?). Christ Church and the Kentish minsters lost goods in these years (Kirby, p. 178 (?)). Fugitives taken off the beaches, plunder sold by spearmen and the king's corn boats in the Wantsum are ours. People: Beornheah, a thegn of the Marsh, is invented (Beorn- + -heah). Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_10 and one of ch_kentish_revolt_796_ferried, ch_kentish_revolt_796_ferried_paid, ch_kentish_revolt_796_loot, ch_kentish_revolt_796_piloted.

cards.note: Ending 1, what happened (drawn at Sarre or Fordwic from September 798 to 800, for anyone who went through step 10 without taking Kent's side). Cuthred, Coenwulf's brother, is king of Kent; the archbishop is home; the land is burnt and wants corn. Sources: Cuthred king of Kent 798 to 807 (in charters by 801, Kirby p. 179); Aethelheard back at Canterbury (he goes to Rome in 801); toll freedom for a named ship at Sarre and Fordwic by a king's writing (Sawyer 29, King Eadberht II for Minster in Thanet, 763 or 764: dossiers/sarre.md), given to minsters as far as the charters show, so a merchant's is the game's stretch (?). People: Cuthred's reeve and the archbishop's clerk are invented and unnamed. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_end_mercia and ch_kentish_revolt_796_done, and one or two of unlock_charter_sarre, unlock_title_archbishops_man, unlock_charter_fordwic, unlock_plot_sarre.

cards.note: Ending 2, what happened, from the losing side (drawn at Quentovic or Dofras from September 798 to 800, for a man who took Kent's side and never the reeve's). The Kentish who got away settle what they owe. Sources: Kent laid waste and its king led away bound (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 796 for 798); exiles from English kingdoms lived under King Charles's protection (Charles to Offa, 796); a sworn partnership in a boat is the Norse felag of CHAINS.md, among the English a sworn fellowship (?); the Wantsum and the Stour mouth as waters to be learned (dossiers/sarre.md). That Kentish thegns fled to Quentovic in 798 is ours (?). People: Beornheah as step 10. Sets ch_kentish_revolt_796_end_kent, ch_kentish_revolt_796_done and the lasting cost ch_kentish_revolt_796_mercia_remembers, and one or two of unlock_partner_beornheah, unlock_pilot_wantsum, unlock_ship_coaster_minster_ship.

thegn.note: Beornheah, the thegn of the Marsh, landless now; invented

cards.title: What Kent owes
cards.intention: The thegn of the Marsh finds your boat before you have made fast. He has a sea chest, a boy of twelve, and a way of standing that says the chest is all of it.

options.label: Swear fellowship with him: his chest and his knowledge of the coast in a second boat
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_kent.out_partner (the honest road: 600 d and two grand rewards; only for the man who took people off the beach for nothing)

options.label: Take his coaster, got out of the Stour before the burning, against all that is owed
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_kent.out_keel (finale: a ship and 250 d)

options.label: Take the last of his wool and be shown the swatchways of the Wantsum
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_kent.out_wool (finale: thirty bolts, worth about 540 d, 100 d, and the water)

memory.keel: took the coaster for the debt
memory.wool: took the wool and the knowledge of the Wantsum

cards.note: Ending 3, the two-faced man's reckoning (drawn at Lundenwic from September 798 to 800, for a man who served the reeve and armed or warned Kent). The reeve lays two tallies side by side. Sources: London burned in 798 with great loss of life (Historia Regum 798; chronicle_793.json 798-london-fire-798), so the wic wants timber, corn and men who can find them; seized ships sold by a king's reeve are ours (?). Cast: cast.wighelm. cards.title: Two tallies, side by side
cards.intention: The Strand smells of wet ash. The reeve has two tally sticks on the table in the king's hall: what you did for his king, and what you did for the other one.

options.label: Buy his silence with names: who in Kent ordered iron, and who paid
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_both.out_names (finale: 800 d and a man on the Strand; the cost is said first in reeve_warn)

options.label: Buy the Kentish trader he took at Fordwic, at a tenth of her worth
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_both.out_hull (finale: a sea-going ship worth several thousand for 300 d)

options.label: Say a merchant sells to whoever stands on the beach, and wait
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_both.out_plain (costs pride only: 600 d of earnest for the burnt wic's corn, and the reeve's leave to keep using the water you learned)

memory.plain: said a merchant sells to whoever stands on the beach

cards.note: Ending 4, history changed (scheduled 40 days after step 9 at Fordwic; also drawn there to 800). Eadberht has laid the kingdom down and gone over the water, the Mercian king comes into Kent without burning it, and the archbishop comes home. What really happened is ending 1. Sources for what stays true: Cuthred king of Kent 798 to 807; Aethelheard archbishop to 805; Pope Leo's refusal to move the see (798). Invented: all the rest. Cast: cast.aethelheard. cards.title: Roofs still on
cards.intention: The landing below Canterbury is as it was: thatch on the halls, corn in the ricks, one man at the toll bench. The archbishop has walked down from the city himself to see a Frisian boat come in.

options.label: Ask the archbishop's protection, and a keel free of toll at Fordwic
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_spared.out_writing (hard road: 1,200 d and two grand rewards)

options.label: Ask ground by the Stour and a clerk of the church to keep your goods there
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_spared.out_ground (hard road: 900 d and two grand rewards)

options.label: Ask only what the abbess's ships have at Sarre, and give a tenth of the gift to the poor of Kent
options.note: outcome: chain_kentish_revolt_796.end_spared.out_little (hard road: 600 d, two grand rewards and a good name)
